body.statement: Suppose \(E\ge d+1\) and positive \(q,L,\eta,\sigma_t^2,\sigma_y^2\) satisfy \(a_0+\rho\le1\le a_1-\rho\), \(q_0+\rho\le q\le q_1-\rho\), \(q/2\le B-\rho\), \(\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\ge\kappa_0+\rho\), and the \(2R_{\max}+\delta\)-moment maximum displayed in the explicit Poisson--Gaussian witness is at most \(M-\rho\).  For the resulting \(\theta\), every \(k\ge2\) obeys \(u_k=\eta(1^k,\ldots,d^k,0,\ldots,0)^\top\) and \(c_k=u_k\).  The leading \(d\times d\) block of \(C\) is \(\eta V_d=\eta[j^k]_{j=1,\ldots,d;\ k=2,\ldots,d+1}\), which is nonsingular because it is a Vandermonde matrix after factoring \(j^2\) from row \(j\); moreover \(\sigma_d(C)\ge\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\ge\kappa_0+\rho\).  Consequently \(A=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_d\}\), every \(c_k\) lies in \(A\), and \(r^\star(\theta)=\infty\).  Under \(S\), the invariant Gaussian treatment source is the latent source, so every latent cumulant-shift vector is zero, while the observed \(C\) is unchanged and \(r^\star(S\theta)=\infty\).  In both representations, \(T_e=\epsilon_{u,e}+\epsilon_{t,e}\) and \(Y_e=(q/2)\epsilon_{u,e}-(q/2)\epsilon_{t,e}+\epsilon_y\), whereas the effects are respectively \(-q/2\) and \(q/2\).  Thus \(\theta,S\theta\in\Theta_\rho^\circ\), they generate the same \(P_e\) in every environment, \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\), and \(\mathcal N_\rho\ne\varnothing\) for every compatible collection of bounds satisfying these feasibility conditions.
body.justification: The explicit scaled-Vandermonde construction proves that the source-swap branch contains interior unequal-effect laws whenever the fixed bounds are jointly feasible.
body.gap: Kivva et al.'s two-environment swap supplies the algebraic ambiguity, but it does not establish nonvacuity of this calibrated \(d\)-plane, fixed-gap, bounded-moment interior domain.
body.consumer: The proposition ensures that the no-breakout verdict used for a Sachs edge corresponds to an attainable simultaneous-shift model rather than a branch created only by set notation.
